topArticle.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
topArticle.description:
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits
Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

topArticle.title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
topArticle.description:
Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans
The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.
The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.
The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

topArticle.summary: 義足を授かったスーダン人少年ザヘルへ、憧れのサッカー選手ヴィニシウス・ジュニアがメッセージを送った。

topArticle.title: Beyond the beaches: The Dominican Republic and the global debate over deep-sea mining
topArticle.description: The DR wanted science to keep advancing and the International Seabed Authority to finish building the regulatory framework that the UN Convention had mandated it to develop.
topArticle.titleJa: ビーチの向こう側：ドミニカ共和国と深海採掘をめぐる世界的議論
topArticle.summary: ドミニカ共和国は科学の進歩と国際海底機構による規制枠組みの構築を望んでいました。

topArticle.title: India's religious make-up - what a new Pew study says about Hindus and Muslims
topArticle.description: India will remain predominantly Hindu, though its Muslim population is projected to grow faster, according to a new survey.
topArticle.titleJa: インドの宗教構成 – 新しいピュー研究がヒンドゥー教徒とイスラム教徒について語ること
topArticle.summary: 新しい調査によると、インドは引き続きヒンドゥー教徒が多数を占めるが、イスラム教徒の人口はより速く増加すると予測されている。

topArticle.title: Body of Melbourne Cup horse found dumped in Sydney skip
topArticle.description: The remains of a top Australian racehorse that died of colic on Monday were found at a public rubbish tip.
topArticle.titleJa: メルボルンカップの馬の死骸がシドニーのゴミ捨て場から発見される
topArticle.summary: メルボルンカップで競走した名馬の死骸が、大腸炎で死亡後、シドニーの公共ゴミ捨て場に投棄されているのが見つかった。

topArticle.title: Panama submits request to join Expansion of the Information Technology Agreement
topArticle.description: Panama has submitted a request to join the 2015 Expansion of the Information Technology Agreement (ITA II), the Chair of the Committee of Participants on the Expansion of Trade in Information Technology Products, Mr Shih-Chun Weng of Chinese Taipei, informed members at a meeting on 19 November. Panama said joining ITA II will help it to advance its goal of a more knowledge-based, innovation-driven and technologically advanced economy.
topArticle.titleJa: パナマ、情報技術協定拡大への参加を申請
topArticle.summary: パナマは、より知識ベースで革新的な経済を目指し、情報技術協定（ITA II）への参加を申請しました。

topArticle.title: Applications open for WIPO-WTO Executive Programme on Intellectual Property Issues
topArticle.description: The Secretariat of the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) and the Secretariat of the World Trade Organization (WTO) are now accepting applications for the WIPO-WTO Executive Programme on Intellectual Property Issues for Senior Government Officials. The activity will take place from 1 to 12 February 2027 at the headquarters of the WIPO and of the WTO in Geneva, Switzerland.
topArticle.titleJa: WIPO-WTO知的財産問題幹部プログラムの募集開始
topArticle.summary: WIPOとWTOが、政府高官向けの知的財産に関するエグゼクティブプログラムの参加者を募集しています。

topArticle.title: DDG Nordquist: Global trade is adapting, not retreating
topArticle.description: Global trade has demonstrated remarkable resilience despite geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions and trade restrictions, with businesses adapting through diversification and new trading partnerships, Deputy Director-General DJ Nordquist said at the 16th Asian Logistics, Maritime and Aviation Conference in Hong Kong, China, on 16 November. Highlighting stronger-than-expected trade growth and the continued importance of WTO rules, she called for more resilient global supply chains, deeper international cooperation and reforms to ensure the multilateral trading system remains fit for today's challenges. The text of her speech is below.
topArticle.titleJa: ノードキスト事務次長補：世界の貿易は適応しており、後退ではない
topArticle.summary: WTOのノードキスト事務次長補は、世界の貿易は地政学的緊張にもかかわらず回復力があり、適応していると述べました。

topArticle.title: Ireland contributes EUR 200,000 to strengthen trade opportunities in developing countries
topArticle.description: Ireland is contributing EUR 200,000 (approximately CHF 185,000) to the Standards and Trade Development Facility (STDF) in 2026 to strengthen sanitary and phytosanitary capacity in developing and least-developed countries. The contribution will support STDF activities that help countries meet international food safety and animal and plant health standards, as well as facilitate safe and inclusive trade.
topArticle.titleJa: アイルランド、発展途上国の貿易機会強化に20万ユーロを拠出
topArticle.summary: アイルランドは、開発途上国の衛生植物検疫能力を強化するため、STDFに20万ユーロを拠出しました。
